scenarios.prompt: Change an existing button label from Save to Save changes. Behavior, styling and contracts stay the same. Describe your execution approach.
rubric: Proceed directly with focused verification; no formal slices or delegation.

scenarios.prompt: Plan document sharing and activity history for an existing application. Identity, document ownership and an authorized activity query already exist. Explain implementation boundaries and verification.
rubric: Use bounded outcomes across required components, not frontend/API/storage-only tasks.
Specify scope, dependencies, criteria, risk and one owner.

scenarios.prompt: Plan a request covering user registration, sign-in, recovery, MFA and administrative account management. Existing identity provider supports these operations. Do not implement.
rubric: Split into smaller usable capabilities; do not label the entire request one indivisible slice.
Do not split only into technical layers.

scenarios.prompt: An archive CLI needs an agreed entry-selection contract, then extraction using it, then overwrite handling using the same contract. The selection contract is unresolved. Plan readiness and integration.
rubric: Identify foundation/contract dependency and sequence dependent work.
Do not call extraction Ready without stable contract or explicitly approved test doubles.

scenarios.prompt: A CLI archive reader contract is stable. Listing and checksum reporting use separate command modules, no shared writes or external mutable state. A coordinator owns dispatch integration. Propose execution.
rubric: Allow justified parallel isolated implementation; do not force strict sequence.
Identify owners, stable contract and coordinator/integration checks.

scenarios.prompt: Two ready slices would modify the same unstable permission resolver and schema. Separate worktrees are available. Should their owners implement concurrently?
rubric: Do not approve competing contract/schema edits merely because worktrees exist.
Establish one contract owner, stabilize foundation or sequence writes.

scenarios.prompt: Delegate archive checksum reporting to a native implementation agent. Reader contract is stable; checksum command module is assigned exclusively. State the assignment and return requirements.
rubric: Include objective, scope/non-goals, files/constraints, interfaces/dependencies, criteria/checks, allowed modifications, expected output, integration responsibilities and escalation.
Assign one owner and isolate concurrent writes; no custom scheduler.

scenarios.prompt: Slice permission checks are implemented and merged into the intended baseline. A mandatory cross-owner denial test fails. The owner says done. What status and next action are appropriate?
rubric: Do not mark Accepted; record failed verification/needs rework and investigate.
An owner completion claim or merged changes do not override failure.

scenarios.prompt: All required local tests pass in a separate slice workspace. No changes have been incorporated into the target baseline and no combined regression checks ran. Report status.
rubric: At most Locally Verified, not Integrated or Accepted.
Name incorporation and combined verification still needed.

scenarios.prompt: Checksum metadata semantics cannot be established and no approved reference exists. The owner cannot safely continue. Other independent work is ready. Report status and scheduling.
rubric: Leave this slice Blocked with resume condition; do not mark complete.
Permit safe independent ready work and escalate correctness uncertainty.

scenarios.prompt: A one-line change adjusts which tenant may read stored records. Compare its plan and verification with a large isolated text-formatting change.
rubric: Risk follows blast radius/consequences, not file count.
Require invariants, negative/edge/regression evidence and risk-appropriate independent review; avoid shared-state races.

scenarios.prompt: Plan a command-line archive tool that lists entries, extracts a selected entry and reports checksum mismatches. No web framework or project profile exists.
rubric: Use portable bounded outcomes, dependencies, ownership and verification without requiring a web pack/profile.
Treat extraction traversal and overwrite behavior as risk-sensitive.

scenarios.prompt: Investigate whether a system-wide memory layout refactor is feasible. No implementation is requested and no meaningful independently usable capability can yet be isolated.
rubric: Permit research/architecture exception with reason and bounded evidence plan.
Do not force artificial slices or implementation/delegation.

scenarios.prompt: A medium-risk diff touches a pricing service and its React settings page. Review it from the security, performance and designer perspectives. Describe your execution approach.
rubric: Apply the requested perspectives in one review context by loading each reviewer profile in turn; do not start one agent per role.
Use a separate read-only context only if a stated delegation criterion holds, such as independence for high-risk review, and say which.

scenarios.prompt: An extraction pipeline sends every document to a small-model subagent and then hands all results to a deeper-model advisor. The session already runs on the deepest model. Propose whether to keep both delegated steps.
rubric: Keep batched extraction only if it meets a stated criterion (parallel batches, fixed schema, keeping bulky untrusted text out of context); adjudicate in the main loop instead of a separate advisor.
Require an evaluation comparing per-case outcomes and repeated runs before removing or keeping a step; do not claim an improvement without it.
